question: Should OpenClaw send these HealthKit aggregates to any user-configured AI provider, and does that provider path satisfy the project's privacy policy and Apple's health, motion, or fitness service restriction?
rationale: The code minimizes the data, but accepting the third-party provider purpose, retention, disclosure, and App Store compliance boundary requires explicit product, security, and release-owner intent.

options.title: Approve a constrained health service
options.body: Ship after limiting the feature to user-requested health/fitness summaries, fixing command setup, completing privacy disclosures, and proving the signed-device flow.

options.title: Restrict eligible provider paths
options.body: Expose Health summaries only through provider configurations or contracts maintainers explicitly approve for HealthKit-derived data.

options.title: Do not ship HealthKit
options.body: Keep the capability out of App Store builds if the project cannot confidently own the provider and retention boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve a constrained health service
recommendation.body: Ship after limiting the feature to user-requested health/fitness summaries, fixing command setup, completing privacy disclosures, and proving the signed-device flow.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the feature sponsor and has recent merged history in the gateway setup path that participates in the blocking configuration behavior.
